result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
I couldn't judge whether the fix worked: no work order on Transformer 1 has been closed, so there's no completed job to check. I also couldn't run the anomaly model, and the fault classification had to be done by hand.

**Work order check:** Transformer 1 at site MAIN has three work orders, all still open. So there's no number, completion date, resolution notes or failure code to report, and no fault that a job was meant to fix.

| WO | Description | Status | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection (suspected contact wear/coking) | Waiting approval, priority 1 | none |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check (thermal fault) | Approved, priority 3 | FC006 (overheating) |
| 1000053 | Corrective oil treatment, degassing or filtration | Waiting approval, priority 2 | none |

Because no oil filtration, degassing or regeneration was completed, gas levels haven't been reset. I used absolute levels and all 4 samples from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18.

**Gas readings (ppm):**

| Date | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| 01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| 01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| 01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |

**Anomaly screen (hydrogen, acetylene, CO): not run.**
- The model catalog has no anomaly detection models.
- The model tools need a data file, and none holds these readings. I have no way to create one here.
- I didn't substitute a fixed threshold, as you asked.
- Looking at the numbers only, there's no step change: H2 stays within about 4% (2800–2950), C2H2 within 6–8 and CO within 30–35.
- The levels themselves are very high, though. H2 is about 2900 ppm and C2H2 is 7 ppm.

**Fault classification (latest complete sample, 2024-01-18):** the classification tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I worked out the ratios by hand using the IEC 60599 method.
- C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 (under 0.1)
- CH4/H2 = 2.53 (over 1)
- C2H4/C2H6 = 3.05 (between 1 and 4)
- **Result: a thermal fault at 300–700 °C (IEC class T2), close to the boundary with the highest-temperature class (T3, above 700 °C).** There is no sign of arcing or partial discharge.
- Because no job was completed, there's nothing to compare this against.

I didn't create a work order, since no job has been completed that a follow-up could reference. The existing open orders 1000052 (retest) and 1000053 (oil treatment) already cover this thermal fault. To get an actual verdict, one of them would need to be completed, then post-job samples screened once the anomaly model has a data file to run on.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly identified that no closed work order exists on Transformer 1 (all three are WAPPR/APPR), correctly took the no-fix-verdict branch, pulled the right six gases for the 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 window, and its hand-computed IEC 60599 ratios (C2H2/C2H4=0.0004, CH4/H2=2.53, C2H4/C2H6=3.05 -> T2) are arithmetically and diagnostically correct against the retrieved data. It also correctly refrained from creating a work order. However, the required anomaly screen on hydrogen, acetylene and CO was not actually executed with a detection model; the agent reports that tsfm.find_models returned no anomaly models and that run_recipe needed a data file, but the visible trace is truncated and only shows wo.list_workorders and iot.history, so the tsfm and fmsr attempts cannot be confirmed. The agent should have tried harder to satisfy the anomaly step (e.g., querying find_models with task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection' explicitly, checking whether iot.history output can be persisted/referenced as a data source, or retrying run_recipe with the asset/sensor identifiers) and should have called iot.stream_extent to confirm the sample range. With the anomaly model result missing, the output for the no-closed-WO branch is incomplete, though the response is honest about the gaps and contains no fabricated results.
